section_summary.extract_value: This abstract describes a two-study investigation of the relationship between appearance goals for exercise and body image. Study 1 (n=215 female UK students, ages 17-30) used a cross-sectional design to examine how appearance goals indirectly negatively associate with body image through introjected (guilt-based) exercise regulation. Study 2 (n=165, ages 18-27) experimentally manipulated guilt and appearance goals to test whether guilt increases body anxiety, finding that guilt manipulation significantly increased post-test guilt and body anxiety among participants in the guilt condition.
section_summary.evidence_source: Abstract text describing both Study 1 and Study 2 methodologies and findings.
